newsitem.title: USA: W. Virginia governor says budget will be tight.
newsitem.headline: W. Virginia governor says budget will be tight.

text.p: West Virginia Gov. Cecil Underwood, scheduled to outline his proposed $2.3 billion budget in a Wednesday night state-of-the state speech, said there would be little room to negotiate because revenues were tight.
"It's so tight, there's not much room for flexibility," Underwood told the Daily Mail Capitol Reporter. "Mostly the budget is commited by statute."
The state expects revenue growth of about $80 million from its expanding tax base, plus a $5 million lottery surplus.

But most the revenue increase may already be claimed as lawmakers take steps to shore up the state's Teachers Retirement System and Public Employees Insurance Agency, and try to keep pace with escalating Medicaid costs.

The newly elected Republican governor has said the biggest challenge will be hammering out a spending proposal for the Department of Health and Human Resources, which oversees Medicaid and other social programs.
